statement: Top-1% wealth share at 2027Q4 >= 2025Q4 + 1 pp (Federal Reserve Distributional Financial Accounts, 2027Q4 release)
status_at_phase_end: Latest DFA vintage (2026-09-18): Bloc A top-1% share of household net worth 32.5% in Q2 2026, a series record; 2025Q4 baseline 31.8% in the same vintage, so the +1 pp threshold would be 32.8%. Quarterly values are revised with each vintage; earlier-vintage readings not separately archived here.

items.summary: Bloc A central-bank distributional accounts: top-1% share of household net worth reached 32.5% in Q2 2026, the highest since the series began in 1989; up 0.8 pp from Q1 2026 and 0.7 pp above the 2025Q4 baseline.
items.detail: Federal Reserve Board DFA, FRED series WFRBST01134, updated 2026-09-18 (Bloc A). Values in this vintage: Q2 2025 31.1, Q3 2025 31.5, Q4 2025 31.8, Q1 2026 31.7, Q2 2026 32.5.

items.summary: Q1 2026 distributional accounts reading: top-1% net-worth share 31.7%, marginally below the 2025Q4 level (31.8%).
items.detail: FRED/ALFRED WFRBST01134 Q1 2026 value as shown in the 2026-09-18 vintage (Bloc A). Exact Q1 release date not verified (DFA typically follows the Z.1 release in mid-June); the value at first publication may differ slightly.

items.summary: 2025Q4 baseline reading of the top-1% net-worth share: 31.8% (current vintage), defining the +1 pp threshold at about 32.8%.
items.detail: FRED WFRBST01134 Q4 2025 value in the 2026-09-18 vintage (Bloc A). Q4 data first published with the March 2026 Z.1/DFA update; exact date and first-vintage value not verified.

items.summary: Same release: top-1% held 50.9% of corporate equities and mutual-fund shares; bottom 50% held 2.3% of net worth; top-1% share up 1.4 pp year on year, attributed mainly to equity-price gains.
items.detail: Federal Reserve DFA Q2 2026 (Bloc A), FRED WFRBST01122 (equities share 50.9). Secondary summary by 24/7 Wall St (2026-11-14) cross-checked against FRED release table.

items.summary: No quarterly distributional wealth series comparable to the Bloc A accounts exists for Bloc B; the indicator relies on a single-jurisdiction source.
items.detail: Federal Reserve DFA covers the Bloc A only; Bloc B publishes no official quarterly wealth-distribution series (only irregular survey/academic estimates).
